SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

2. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. A — newton (N)

5. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. B — Producers

7. C — Ice melting to water

8. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

10. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. D — Glucose and oxygen

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
